app/package.json:11-12 — react-router 1.170.46 / react-start 1.169.4, latest stable (2026-10-22 release)
app/vite.config.ts:1-10 — no experimental config flags; grep over app/ finds no unstable_/experimental_ names
reach.rationale: Exactly one RC dependency (Nitro v3), but it sits in the central build/serve path; the rest of the app uses only current-stable framework APIs.

evidence: app/vite.config.ts:2,9 — the only two source references to nitro (one import, one plugin entry)
app/package.json:21 — devDependency, not a runtime dep

containment.rationale: The RC is confined to package.json and one plugin line in vite.config.ts; no application source touches it, so swapping or upgrading it touches two files.

evidence: app/package.json:7 — "start": "node .output/server/index.mjs" requires a Nitro-built server bundle
app/vite.config.ts:9 — nitro() matches TanStack Start's documented Node.js/Docker hosting recipe verbatim
app/src/lib/queries.ts:13 — .validator() is the current stable createServerFn API (inputValidator is the deprecated alias)
justification.rationale: Nitro is the sanctioned (and effectively only documented) adapter for a self-hosted Node production server; the rest of the app uses stable APIs and reaches for nothing experimental for novelty.

findings.issue: Production server layer is built on nitro 3.0.261029-rc, a release candidate published the day before this review; TanStack's hosting docs note the nitro/vite integration is 'still under active development'.
findings.suggestion: Acceptable since it is the documented path, but plan the bump to nitro 3.0.0 stable as soon as it ships and keep the lockfile pinned (it already is) so RC updates are deliberate.

findings.issue: The whole toolchain is at the freshest possible versions (react-start 1.169.4 and react-router 1.170.46 released 2026-10-22, nitro RC 2026-10-29), so nothing has had time to soak.
findings.suggestion: Fine for a greenfield app with a committed lockfile; just watch the TanStack/router changelog for early regressions on the next patch wave.

summary: The app leans on exactly one non-stable dependency — the Nitro v3 RC — and places it precisely where TanStack Start's own hosting docs put it, isolated to two files with no application-source coupling. Everything else (router, Start, React 19, Vite 8) is current stable, and the only recently-renamed API it uses, createServerFn().validator(), is the forward-compatible side of the rename. Risk is low and confined: the production-server layer is a brand-new RC with no soak time.
